clue.text: Lady on the sun deck causes confusion

parts.note: Di is a short woman's name, a common crossword lady
S is the standard abbreviation for sun
to deck is to dress up or adorn, as to array

explanation.surface: A woman lounging on a sunny ship's deck is making a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' just puts DI above the rest. 'Deck' looks like part of a ship but is the verb meaning to dress up.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of disorder or muddle is a straightforward synonym for confusion.

clue.text: Request money up front, mostly

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' puts the money on top, ahead of the next piece

parts.note: P stands for penny or pence, so small money

indicators.note: mostly says most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to be in the lead is to be in front

explanation.surface: Someone asks for payment in advance, or nearly all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up front' reads as advance payment, but 'up' places P at the top and 'front' is LEAD, trimmed to LEA by 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeal or entreaty is a synonym for a request.

clue.text: Restrain Greek character who's raring to go outside

indicators.note: outside says the eager word is wrapped around the Greek letter

parts.note: someone raring to go is eager, keen
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Holding back a Greek who is itching to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in is to hold it back or suppress it, so to restrain.

clue.text: Common sense we expressed in French

explanation.surface: Practical wisdom, as a French speaker would say 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical intelligence is the British informal sense of the Greek-derived word; it is also the French first-person plural pronoun.

clue.text: Felt upper chest initially becoming tense

indicators.note: becoming says these letters turn into something else, a rearrangement
initially takes the first letter of chest

explanation.surface: Someone felt their upper chest at first becoming tight with tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' rearranges FELT, UPPER and C (the first letter of 'chest'). 'Tense' looks like an adjective about the chest but is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The past perfect (had done) is a grammatical tense, also called by this Latin-derived name.

clue.text: Good person can switch to key position

parts.note: St is short for saint, a good person

indicators.note: switch says the letters of the word can change places

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A kind soul can change to a crucial role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like crucial, as in key position, but it is a musical key; 'switch' is the anagram signal on 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: One's stance is one's posture or stated attitude, so a position.

clue.text: Lines of communication?

parts.note: read literally, lines spoken to each other by characters in a play or film, rather than routes for messages

explanation.surface: Channels by which messages pass between parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversation written as spoken lines in a script is exactly what lines of communication would be, taken literally.

clue.text: Book a restaurant meal that isn't beyond one's reach

explanation.surface: Reserving a place to eat when it is within your grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it means to reserve a place at a restaurant; as one word it is an adjective meaning reachable or accessible.

clue.text: None chance putting money in, recently

parts.note: none is nought, written as the letter O

indicators.note: putting ... in says one piece is placed inside another
with putting, it says the money goes inside the chance word

parts.note: fate is fortune or chance
L is the old abbreviation for pounds, money

explanation.surface: Lately, with nothing left to chance, someone has been investing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting money in' reads as investing, but it puts L inside FATE to make FLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately, in the recent past, is what the two-word phrase means.

clue.text: Sounds like a moment to anticipate

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is a word pronounced the same as the phrase meaning a moment

parts.note: moment can mean importance or weight, as in a matter of great moment

explanation.surface: Something that seems like a brief instant to look forward to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A moment' looks like a short time, A WAIT, but it is A WEIGHT: moment in the sense of importance; spoken aloud they match.
explanation.definitionFit: To look forward to or expect something is to anticipate it.

clue.text: Stay after person keeps quiet

parts.note: post is a prefix meaning after
p is the musical abbreviation piano, quiet
one can mean a person, as in one never knows

explanation.surface: Staying on after someone keeps their mouth shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' is the verb as in a stay of execution, to put off.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay a decision or execution is to delay or defer it.

clue.text: Minster tries preaching differently

definitions.note: the printed text is a misreading of minister, a member of the clergy

indicators.note: differently says the letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A clergyman tries delivering sermons in a new style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Differently' rearranges the two words 'tries preaching'; 'Minster' reads as a cathedral but stands for a clergyman here.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman with charge of a parish or church is a minister, a vicar in charge of the parish.

clue.text: Female runner ?

parts.note: not an athlete but a woman sent to run messages and small tasks

explanation.surface: A woman who races.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl employed to run small tasks and messages runs, but for her employer, not in a race.

clue.text: Be imaginative but get over ambitious

explanation.surface: Be creative, yet aim too high.
explanation.definitionFit: Having thoughts and notions is being imaginative; to have notions above one's station is to grow too ambitious.

clue.text: African sport a youth's backing out of

indicators.note: out of says the reversed pair stands around the sport
backing says the pair of words are read back to front

parts.note: taken as written
a youth is a boy; the 's is a link
RU is short for Rugby Union, a sport

explanation.surface: A sport that young people are pulling out of in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reverses both 'a' and the youth, and 'out of' puts that reversal around the sport; 'sport' looks like the definition but 'African' is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yoruba are a West African people, chiefly of Nigeria, so the word can name an African.

clue.text: Number contend with party in Northern Spain

parts.note: zero is a number, written as the letter O
to vie is to compete or contend
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Several compete with a political party in the north of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political but is DO, a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Asturias is one place in the north of Spain.

clue.text: Gold label's stuck on National Trust figure

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a name is a label; the 's is a link
NT is short for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A golden tag is stuck on a statue owned by the National Trust, Britain's conservation charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative figurine standing on a shelf is a figure in the sense of a small statue.

clue.text: Hands-on experience for young artists ?

parts.note: taken literally, hands put on the paint by children making pictures, not practical training

explanation.surface: Practical training for budding painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children make pictures with their fingers dipped in colour, a literally hands-on activity.

clue.text: Church is cross about being under duress

indicators.note: about says the crossing word goes around the church

parts.note: a ford is a place to cross a river; to ford is to cross
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church is angry about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is the verb FORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Done under compulsion or coercion is done under duress.

clue.text: Mean to drink up and go

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Meaning to finish one's drink and leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink up and go' reads as leaving a pub, but 'up' turns LAP over.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of small or stingy is a synonym for petty, meagre.

clue.text: Root about and left with novel

parts.note: the root of something is its source or origin
a. is an abbreviation of about, as in dates

explanation.surface: Someone rummages and is left holding a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root about' reads as rummaging and 'novel' as a book, but 'novel' is the adjective, new.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel as an adjective means new and fresh, unlike anything before.

clue.text: Architect emerges from Joanna's house

indicators.note: emerges from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An architect comes out of a woman's home.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash was the Regency designer of London's Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion.

clue.text: Energy's thus channelled into premier racecourse

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy; 's is the link is

indicators.note: channelled into says one word is fed inside another

parts.note: PM, prime minister, is the premier
so means thus

explanation.surface: Power directed into the top racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs, in Surrey, is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey course where the Derby is run is a famous racecourse.

clue.text: Yet takes time out supporting member

indicators.note: takes ... out says a letter is removed
with takes, removal of the time letter

parts.note: still means yet, as in still to come

explanation.surface: Even so, someone takes time away from backing a club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like a person but is a structural part.
explanation.definitionFit: A window ledge is a horizontal beam bearing weight, a supporting member in building.

clue.text: Central parts of a Southern county, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is pronounced like the county's short name

parts.note: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, a county north of London in southern England

explanation.surface: The middle bits of a county in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: HERTS, Hertfordshire's abbreviation, is said the same as HEARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or centre of something is its heart, so central parts.

clue.text: Rex said no, being worried about trainee girl

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the trainee
being worried says the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner, a trainee, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Rex said no, anxious about a girl in training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being worried' rearranges SAID NO to OSAIND, which goes 'about' L. Rex looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, borne by the heroine of As You Like It.
